observations_for_tool_builders: Upstream smc_feynman_kac computes nll0 = -logsumexp(log_g0(samples0)) without subtracting log(nparticles) (feynman_kac.py lines 82-85), while later steps use normalised weights. The returned PF nll is therefore offset by -log(nparticles) relative to the standard bootstrap estimate of -log p(y_0:N): adding log(1000)=6.9078 gives multinomial 141.2841, stratified 141.3712, systematic 141.6051, diffusion euler 142.1316 / lord_and_rougemont 143.1145 / jentzen_and_kloeden 143.2623 / tweedie 141.2966, ensemble_ot 138.4736 vs KF 141.4217. The tests' rtol 5e-2..7e-2 absorbs this ~7-nat offset. Constant offset, so gradients are unaffected. A wrapper reproducing upstream must report the raw upstream value (and may document/also report the corrected value); it must not silently change it.

Margins to the test tolerances are small for diffusion_tweedie (rel err 0.04973 vs rtol 0.05) and ensemble_ot eps=0.1 (0.06969 vs 0.07), i.e. these pass only for this key; other seeds may fail the test tolerances.
multinomial and multinomial_stopped give bitwise-identical forward outputs (differ only in gradients), as the scanner noted.
KF/RTS reproduce the closed-form GP regression to <1e-13 relative (test_kf asserts rtol 1e-7).
